title: Juara Digital Pandai 2026 Winners: The Primary Top 10, in Their Own Words
summary: Meet the Juara Digital Pandai 2026 primary winners in their own words, from Adhan’s reluctant-to-motivated story to the rest of the Top 10.
body_markdown:
On 19 September 2026, the Grand Final of *[Juara Digital Pandai 2026](https://blog.pandai.org/juara-digital-pandai-2026-grand-final/)* brought the country’s top young digital learners onto one stage at SJKC Wu Teck in Klang. Ten of them came from the primary category: the Top 10. Right after the final round, several of the youngest winners shared what the experience gave them. So here are the primary winners, in their own words.


## **Meet Adhan Solihin (6th Place)**


Adhan Solihin, from SK Dato’ Syed Zain Alshahab, finished 6th in the primary category. His is the story that sticks because it is about a change in himself.


*“Dulu saya malas nak belajar, selepasnya saya seronok nak belajar.”* (I used to be lazy about studying; afterwards, I enjoy it.)


What changed the feeling was simple, he said: *“Senang nak belajar dan dengan ada game”* (It’s easy to learn, and there are games). And when he summed up the shift in one line, it was about motivation:


*“Dulu saya tak ada motivasi nak belajar, sekarang saya ada motivasi untuk belajar.”* (I used to have no motivation to study; now I have the motivation to learn.)


## **What the Rest of the Finalists Said**


Across the rest of the primary Top 10, the same theme came through: learning that feels like play.


For Sree Vishnu (5th, SK Bukit Kemuning 2), JDP was a discovery. *“Sebelum JDP, saya tak tahu apa itu JDP, satu perkataan pun tak tahu,”* he recalled, *“tapi apabila saya dengar pasal JDP, saya rasa minat yang sangat seronok untuk main tu”* (Before JDP, I didn’t know what it was at all; but once I heard about it, I felt a real, fun interest in it). The reason was the format: *“Kerana dia buat pembelajaran sambil bermain best”* (Because it makes learning happen while you play).


For Muhammad Syahril Ikram (9th, SK Kuala Klawang), the change showed up in his schoolwork and his self-belief: *“Saya rasa pendidikan saya makin pandai dan makin meningkat”* (I feel my learning is improving), and he came away more confident *“berani, sebab saya makin confident boleh menang lagi”* (brave, because I’m more confident I can win again).


For some, the pleasure was simpler still. Siti Nuraleesya Qaisara (3rd, SK Kampong Ladang) liked that she could learn on the go *“Saya buat quiz sambil saya main game. Sebab saya boleh buat dekat mana-mana je”* (I do quizzes while I play because I can do it anywhere) — and summed up the day in the most natural way a child could: *“Saya rasa seronok lah bila menang”* (I just feel happy when I win).


And Muhammad Adam Haaris (7th, SK Taman Klang Jaya) summed up the appeal simply — *“seimbang dengan dapat main game dan sambil belajar”* (a balance of playing games while learning) before giving the most down-to-earth answer of the day. Asked what he would do with his RM300 prize, he had a plan ready: *“nak guna untuk masuk kelab bola sepak”* (use it to join a football club).


## **What the Juara Digital Pandai 2026 Winners Showed**


Listen to the youngest winners and one thing is clear: they are not describing homework. They are describing something they enjoy. That is exactly what a competition built on quizzes and games is meant to do which is turn learning into a habit children want to keep. For Adhan, it even replaced *“malas”* with motivation. That is the real prize.
